W1: Hi, Tom. Did you get the schedule for next week's training? / M1: Not yet. I checked my email this morning, but nothing's arrived. / W1: Oh, I thought Ms. Park sent it yesterday. I'll forward you my copy. / M1: Thanks. Could you also send me the room number? / W1: Sure. It's room two-fifteen, on the second floor.

M1: Excuse me, is the nine-fifteen train to Newark on time? / W1: I'm afraid it's delayed. There's a signal problem, so it'll leave at ten. / M1: That's forty-five minutes late! I have an interview at ten thirty. / W1: You could take the express from platform fourteen. It leaves at nine thirty.

W1: The printer on the second floor is out of paper again. / M1: I'll get some from the supply room. How many boxes do we have left? / W1: Only two, I think. We should order more before Friday. / M1: Good idea. I'll ask Ms. Gomez to place the order this afternoon.

M1: Hi, Rachel. Are you ready for the client presentation at two? / W1: Almost. The projector in room three-oh-two isn't working, though. / M1: Don't worry. I'll ask the IT department to bring one now. / W1: Thanks. Oh, and could you print twelve copies of the handout? / M1: Sure, I'll do it right away.

W1: Excuse me, does this bus go to the convention center? / M1: No, you'll need the number forty. It stops across the street. / W1: Thanks! How often does it run? / M1: About every fifteen minutes, but it's slower on weekends.

M1: Ms. Wong, the shipment of office chairs was supposed to arrive today, wasn't it? / W1: Yes, but the supplier called this morning. There's been a delay at the port. / M1: Do you know when we'll get them? / W1: They said Wednesday, but I'd better double-check with them tomorrow.

W1: Hello, this is Carla Mendes from Brightwell Dental. I'm calling about the brochures we ordered last week. / M1: Hi, Ms. Mendes. Yes, I have your order here. Is there a problem? / W1: Not exactly. We need them for a health fair on Friday, and I wanted to make sure they'll be ready in time. / M1: They're printed already. I can have them delivered tomorrow afternoon. / W1: That's perfect. Please send them to the front desk.

M1: Hi, Janet. Do you have a minute? I wanted to talk about next week's safety training. / W1: Sure. Is it still on Tuesday morning? / M1: That's the issue. The trainer can't come until Wednesday, so we'll need to move the session. / W1: Wednesday is fine for my team, but a few of us have a client meeting after lunch. / M1: Then let's start at nine. That should finish before noon. / W1: Great. I'll let everyone know.

M1: Good evening. I have a reservation under Daniel Foster. / W1: Welcome, Mr. Foster. I see you're booked for three nights. May I have your credit card for the deposit? / M1: Of course. Also, is breakfast included? I didn't see it on my confirmation. / W1: Breakfast is served from six to ten in the restaurant on the second floor. Here's your key card.

W1: Excuse me, I'm here to pick up a prescription for my son. The last name is Alvarez. / M1: One moment, I'll check. Yes, it's ready, but I'd like to explain something first. The doctor changed the dosage this time. / W1: Thank you. I didn't notice any change. / M1: He should take one tablet in the morning and one at night, with food. / W1: Got it. Do I pay here or at the front counter? / M1: Right here. Your insurance covers most of it, so it's only five dollars.

W1: Mr. Chen, I'm calling to confirm your interview for the marketing position. It's scheduled for Thursday at two o'clock. / M1: Thursday? I thought it was Wednesday. Hold on, let me check my calendar. Oh, you're right, Thursday. Sorry about that. / W1: No problem. Please arrive fifteen minutes early, and bring a copy of your portfolio. / M1: Will I meet with the department head? / W1: Yes, Ms. Okafor will be interviewing you, along with a member of the design team.

M1: Hi, Sandra. I'm ordering supplies for the office. Do we still need to buy printer paper? / W1: Yes. We have only two boxes left, and we use about ten a month. / M1: Okay. The supplier has a sale. If we order twenty boxes, we get a discount. / W1: Twenty is too many for our storage closet. How about fifteen? / M1: Fifteen should be enough. I'll place the order this afternoon and ask them to deliver it on Monday.

W1: Hi, Tom. Are you ready for the client presentation at ten? / M1: Not quite. The projector in Conference Room B isn't turning on, and the client will arrive in twenty minutes. / W1: Let me call the IT department. If they can't fix it, we can use the larger room on the fourth floor. / M1: Good idea. Meanwhile, I'll move my laptop and handouts there just in case.

W1: Hi, I bought these running shoes yesterday, but they're a little tight. Can I exchange them for a larger size? / M1: Certainly. Unfortunately, we're out of that size in black. We have it in gray, though, or we can order black for you. / W1: I really wanted black. How long would it take? / M1: About three days. I can have it shipped to your home so you don't have to come back. / W1: That would be great. Here's my address.

M1: Did you see the email about our office? We're moving to the Harbor Building next month. / W1: I did. I'm happy about it, but I'm worried about the commute. It's much farther from my apartment. / M1: Me too. I heard the company may offer a shuttle bus from the train station. / W1: That would help a lot. I'll ask Human Resources whether it's confirmed.

W1: Marcus, did you finish the budget report? The directors want it by Friday. / M1: Almost. I only need the figures from the sales team, but Priya said they won't be ready until Thursday. / W1: That's cutting it close. Could you ask Priya whether she can send them earlier? / M1: I already did, and she said she'd try for Wednesday evening. I'll review everything on Thursday morning, then submit it. / W1: Perfect. Just let me know if anything changes.

M1: Good morning, Lakeside Catering. How can I help you? / W1: Hi, I'm organizing a retirement party for our accounting department next Saturday. We expect about forty guests, and I'd like to see your menu. / M1: Certainly. We have buffet and sit-down options. For forty people, the buffet is usually more affordable. / W1: Then the buffet sounds right. Could you email me the menu and prices today? / M1: Of course. I just need your email address.

M1: Hi, Yuki. I'm back from the conference in Denver. Where should I submit my travel receipts? / W1: You can upload them to the finance portal, but the deadline for reimbursement is this Friday. / M1: This Friday? Oh, I thought I had until the end of the month. I'd better do it now. / W1: Good idea. If you have trouble with the portal, ask Mr. Hayes in the finance office. He can help you. / M1: Thanks. I'll go to his office after lunch.

W1: Hello, IT help desk. This is Rosa. / M1: Hi, Rosa. I can't log in to the shared drive. It keeps saying my password has expired. / W1: That happens every ninety days. You can reset it through the company website. Do you have the link? / M1: No, I don't. Could you send it to me? / W1: Sure. I'll send it right now. Once you reset it, wait a few minutes before you try again.

M1: Welcome to Greenfield Fitness. Are you interested in a membership? / W1: Yes. I work nearby, so I'd like to come before work. What time do you open? / M1: We open at five thirty on weekdays. Our monthly plan is forty dollars, or you can pay for a full year and get two months free. / W1: The yearly plan sounds good, but I'd like to try the gym first. / M1: No problem. I can give you a free three-day pass. You just need to fill out this form.
